text:
maria-support: heads-up — cust ACME reported p99 spikes from APAC starting ~08:10 UTC, affects their API calls to /v1/generate. They see ~1200ms p99 vs usual ~180ms.

jon-eng-sre: ack. do we have a customer trace? any repro steps?

maria-support: they sent quick curl timings from Tokyo: 
```\ncurl -w "time_namelookup: %{time_namelookup}\ntime_connect: %{time_connect}\ntime_appconnect: %{time_appconnect}\ntime_pretransfer: %{time_pretransfer}\ntime_starttransfer: %{time_starttransfer}\ntotal: %{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
# result total: 1.25
# appconnect: 0.95
```

leah-network: appconnect high usually implies TLS handshake or route hairpin. can you paste a traceroute/tcptraceroute?

maria-support: pasted a short traceroute from their probe (tokyo):
```\ntraceroute to api.redwood.example (13.32.11.9), 30 hops max
 1 10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1) 0.8 ms 0.7 ms 0.6 ms
 2 203.0.113.5 (203.0.113.5) 2.1 ms 2.0 ms 2.2 ms
 3 198.51.100.7 (198.51.100.7) 25.9 ms 26.1 ms 26.0 ms
 4 52.95.12.34 (52.95.12.34) 120.5 ms 119.9 ms 120.1 ms
 5 13.32.11.9 (13.32.11.9) 121.0 ms 120.8 ms 121.2 ms
```

jon-eng-sre: hop 3->4 looks like it jumps to a US POP (120ms). that would explain the added appconnect. anything changed in GSLB weights or any recent DNS TTL flips?

chen-infra: I rolled a small edge routing weight tweak in eu/apac yesterday to balance capacity (rollout id abcd123). TTL unchanged but we did update healthcheck endpoints for a subset of tokyo nodes.

leah-network: probable cause: traffic being steered out-of-region to a US POP due to healthchecks marking APAC hosts unhealthy transiently. check healthcheck logs + route affinity.

maria-support: customer also attached server-side logs showing repeated TLS renegotiation attempts around those request times: "tls: handshake retry after 3 attempts"

jon-eng-sre: can we repro from our TOK probes? i'll run a curl from tokyo probe and tcpdump on candidate POPs.

routebot: probe: tokyo-1 -> api.redwood.example : p95 1.18s, p50 210ms, p99 1.32s (2026-03-17T08:12:10Z)

jon-eng-sre: running tcpdump on apac-pop01... grabbing SNI/TCP handshakes now.

leah-network: check for SYN->RST or SNI mismatch that would trigger fallback to alternate sites. Also confirm if any GSLB backend flapping events around 08:08-08:15.

chen-infra: healthcheck logs show 5xx responses from apac-backend-3 between 08:07 and 08:09 (short window) — automatically marked unhealthy for ~120s then recovered. that would cause weight to drop and some clients to failover to US POP.

maria-support: customer timeline matches — spike started 08:10 and lasted ~6 minutes. they had 40% of requests routed to us-east via that window.

jon-eng-sre: mitigation idea: reduce sensitivity of healthcheck probe (increase consecutive-success threshold) to avoid short flaps, and enable regional affinity override for PLAT tier customers while we stabilize. immediate fix: re-enable apac-backend-3 by manual override so GSLB sees it healthy.

leah-network: agreed. i'll hold manual mark-up for apac-backend-3 and set temporary sticky-affinity for APAC prefix to APAC POPs for 10m.

chen-infra: applied manual put-back on apac-backend-3 (rollout id revert-ef01). healthcheck now returns 200 consistently.

routebot: change: apac-backend-3 state -> healthy (08:18:22Z). GSLB rebalanced weights.

maria-support: customer reports p99 dropped to ~200ms after 08:20. 

jon-eng-sre: will follow up with a short post-incident note, need to track: healthcheck sensitivity + noise suppression, add canary for healthcheck change, and consider sticky-affinity for business-tier customers. also doc the rollback playbook.

leah-network: quick follow-up: network capture showed client SNI was correct; issue was backend returning 503 during update window causing traffic-steer. not TLS bug.

maria-support: customer happy with mitigation and the temporary credits we offered. they asked for RCA.

jon-eng-sre: draft RCA checklist: timeline, root cause (healthcheck-induced GSLB failover), impact (p99 + request fanout to US POP), mitigation (manual restore + affinity override), long-term actions (healthcheck thresholds, canary, observability alert for cross-region hops). I'll push draft to #incidents tomorrow. :memo:

ops-bot: reminder scheduled: run retrospective meeting 2026-03-18 14:00 UTC.

maria-support: thanks team — closing this thread, leaving logs in S3 under s3://redwood-support/cases/ACME/5970000000/ 

jon-eng-sre: +1. adding labels: customer-escalation, networking, mitigated. :white_check_mark:
